text: By the Poincare-Bendixson theorem, chaotic trajectories cannot occur in a smooth autonomous system in the plane.
explanation: In two dimensions the Poincare-Bendixson theorem restricts bounded limit sets to fixed points and closed orbits, so at least three dimensions are needed for a continuous-time system to be chaotic (as in the Lorenz system). Discrete maps, by contrast, can be chaotic in one dimension.
